checkpoint.format: PyTorch zip state_dict despite the .h5 extension (DataParallel 'module.' prefix); latent fp32 weights, binarized at runtime
checkpoint.upstream_hash_published: HF LFS sha256 807030d1...0db9 (re-checked via API and x-linked-etag; matches)
checkpoint.download_status: OK via curl from the HF resolve URL. Re-verified 2026-10-29: local sha256 and size match, and HEAD returns 302 -> 200.
checkpoint.inspection: Re-verified: torch.load weights_only=True OK. 106 tensors, 11,699,624 params, all float32. Keys: module.conv1.weight (64,3,7,7), module.conv1.gain, module.layerX.Y.{move0,move1,move2}.bias (1,C,1,1), .conv1.weight/.gain, .prelu.L_alpha (C,), module.layer{2,3,4}.0.downsample.1.weight/gain, module.fc (1000,512). Rounded L_alpha range -19..6. No standardized latent weight is exactly 0.

models.architecture: ResNet-18-style, one binary 3x3 conv per block, [4,4,4,4] blocks (16 binary 3x3), 7x7 stem + maxpool, alpha=0.25, 3 downsample 1x1 convs

reported_metrics.value: ImageNet top-1 61.39%, 11.70M params (HF model card table). Not re-verified locally.

precision.per_layer: stem: fp ScaledStdConv 7x7 s2 + maxpool. body: 16 binary 3x3 convs (W1A1, per-channel scale*gain). downsample: AvgPool + 1x1 conv with binary weights on fp input (W1A-fp). residual adds fp. LearnableBias and Q_PReLU fp (power-of-2 slopes). head: global avgpool + fp Linear 512->1000. No norm layers.

models.binarization_semantics: Activations: Network/BNN.py:12-13,29-35 use torch.sign, so sign(0)=0. ReActNet_18_Qaw.py:55-56 computes sign(beta*x + bias), with beta>0 fixed per block. Weights: BNN.py:105-118 standardize over (C,H,W) with biased std, multiply by fan-in^-0.5, then the forward value is per-out-channel mean|W_std| * torch.sign(W_std) * learned gain. torch.sign(0)=0 here too. Padding: F.conv2d zero padding (BNN.py:122), so border inputs to the binary conv are 0, not ±1. Block (ReActNet_18_Qaw.py:51-67): move0 -> sign -> binary 3x3 conv -> out*alpha(0.25) + residual -> move1 bias -> Q_PReLU with slope 2^round(L_alpha) (BNN.py:46-54) -> move2 bias. No BatchNorm anywhere. Downsample (ReActNet_18_Qaw.py:95-99) is AvgPool2d(2) + Bconv1x1 applied to the real-valued x, i.e. binary weights on fp activations.
models.input_spec: 224x224 RGB; eval Resize(256)+CenterCrop(224), ToTensor, Normalize mean (0.485,0.456,0.406) std (0.229,0.224,0.225) (Inference/ImageNet.ipynb)

models.architecture: Shortened ReActNet-A backbone (prototype/model/a_3.py stage_out_channel [32,64,128x2,256x2,512x4,1024x1]: FP stem + 9 BasicBlocks) followed by 3 binary-MLP Blocks at 1024 channels (each 3 ShiftBlocks + 1 PointBlock); dual FP heads fc + fc_dist averaged at eval

Downsample: stride-2 binary 3x3 with AvgPool on the residual; channel doubling by concatenating two binary 1x1 branches. Head: avgpool, two FP FCs averaged at eval.

ShiftBlock (l.60-153): the binarized activation is split into 4 channel groups and circularly rolled (torch.roll, wraparound) by +/-1 (Shift) and +/-3 (GlobalShift) along H/W, then fed to 1x1 binary convs whose outputs are summed before BN. No contextual dynamic embedding thresholds in a_3.py (that is BCDNet-B).

Weights of Q-layers are stored already bit-packed: 64 binary weights per uint64 word written with the MXNet float64 type flag (e.g. stage1_unit1_conv1: 64x64x3x3 = 36,864 bits = 576 words). Sign convention for 0 and bit order not checked in the C++ source (smd_hpi/src) - assumption: det_sign(x>=0 -> +1), no scaling factor (scaling_factor attr absent). Binarization = det_sign / bit packing with (x >= 0) -> 1, i.e. sign(0)=+1 (smd_hpi/src/xnor_cpu.h:211-242). Input is im2col-padded with 0 BEFORE binarization, so padded border pixels become +1 (q_convolution-inl.h:216-227 comment "This process should be after padding elem since the padding elements are all 0"). scaling_mode default none (no alpha; q_convolution-inl.h:97-105,184-192). XNOR + popcount GEMM on CPU (xnor_cpu.h).

models.architecture: BNext tiny: stage_out_channel [32,64,128x2,256x2,512x6,1024x2]. feature[0] = FP stem; feature[1..13] = 13 BasicBlocks. Each block = a 3x3 binary unit (ELM 'Attention' class on even indices; FFN_3x3 without the ELM multiply on block 1 and odd indices, both stored under the 'Attention.' prefix) + 1x1 binary FFN, or FFN_1+FFN_2 concatenated when channels double. 31 binary convs.

reported_metrics.value: Top-1 72.4%, 0.077 G BOPs (README table)

precision.per_layer: Stem: FP 3x3 s2 conv + BN (stem PReLU present but unused in forward). Body: all main 3x3 and 1x1 convs binary W1A1. FP: SE branches (avgpool, 1x1 conv+bias, ReLU, 1x1 conv+bias, sigmoid), BN (norm1, norm2), PReLU activation2, Attention.activation1 PReLU on the residual (ELM blocks only), learnable bias 'move', mix scale, elementwise products, residual adds and the concat. Downsample: stride-2 3x3 binary conv with AvgPool2d(2) on the residual; channel doubling by concatenating two same-width binary 1x1 FFNs. Head: PReLU, global avgpool, FP FC.

models.binarization_semantics: src/bnext.py:93-123 HardBinaryConv: temperature<1e-7 gives binary weight = sign(w) with no scale factor (released T ~1e-23). src/bnext.py:72-90 HardSign: sign(clamp(x/max(T,1e-8),-1,1)) = sign(x); torch.sign(0)=0. LearnableBias 'move' (l.59-66) is added before sign as a per-channel threshold. Padding: F.conv2d padding=k//2 on the binarized input, so zeros, which are not in {-1,+1}. Order (Attention l.176-202): residual=PReLU1(in) [avgpooled if s2]; x=BN1(conv(sign(in+b))); PReLU2; mix=scale*in+(1-scale)*x; x=SE(mix)*x; x=x*residual; BN2; +residual. FFN_3x3/FFN_1x1 are the same without the x*residual multiply, and with residual=input.
models.input_spec: 224x224 RGB, timm IMAGENET_DEFAULT mean/std. The official scripts pass --dali_cpu but not --dali, so the timm loader is used: eval crop_pct=0.95 (resize ~235, center crop 224), bicubic interpolation (src/train_assistant_group_amp.py:496-572; src/script/*/run_*.sh). Inferred from code; no standalone eval script.

models.conversion_notes: Custom ops per block: SE with sigmoid, elementwise gating, a learnable mix, two BNs, and an elementwise product with PReLU(input) in ELM blocks. Zero padding of the binary input needs border correction for XNOR-popcount. Drop the temperature buffers and the unused PReLUs. Packed binary weights ~3.5 MB; FP ~2.65M params (~10.6 MB fp32).

models.architecture: Bi-Real Net-18 layout. fp 7x7/2 stem conv + BN + maxpool 3x3/2, no ReLU. 16 binary 3x3 convs, each followed by BN and a real identity add. Downsample = AvgPool2x2 -> fp conv1x1 (no bias) -> BN. Global AvgPool7 -> fp 1x1 conv with bias as fc. Structurally identical to the later official PyTorch birealnet18 (Bi-Real-net commit 2019-11-23). Differs from the official Caffe train prototxt, which has no BN after the downsample conv.

reported_metrics.value: 56.4% top-1 ImageNet; 61.3 ms/image on Google Pixel 1, single thread (daBNN README L43; author claim, not reproduced). 56.4% is identical to the official Bi-Real-18 Caffe result (Bi-Real-net README L76).

precision.per_layer: Stem conv7x7 + BN + maxpool: fp32. Body: 16 binary 3x3 convs, W ±1, activations binarized by the runtime (no explicit Sign in the ONNX); each is followed by fp BN (absorbs scale) and a real-valued residual add. Downsample: AvgPool2x2 -> fp32 conv1x1 -> BN. Head: global avgpool -> fp32 fc (1x1 conv with bias). No attention or LayerNorm.

models.binarization_semantics: Weights are stored as exact ±1 with the scale folded into BN. The ONNX has no Sign ops: onnx2bnn aggressive mode (the default) marks every all-±1 conv as binary (docs/model_conversion.md L37). daBNN runtime padding = -1 on both paths: DIRECT_CONV fills bit 0 via pad.h L11-14, and BGEMM fills float 0 in fused_binarize_im2col.h L37-38, which pack_64 then maps to bit 0 (x > 0 false). daBNN sign(0) is path-dependent: common/common_bitpack.h L26/L110+ uses (x > 0), so 0 -> -1, while the aarch64 pack_128_opt uses sign bit + NOT (dabnn/bitpack.h L117-127), so +0.0 -> +1. The training-time semantics of THESE weights are undocumented. The official Bi-Real Caffe code, the source of the 56.4% figure, binarizes activations with x > 0 ? 1 : -1 (sign(0) = -1; caffe-retrainBN-test/src/caffe/layers/threshold_layer.cpp L20-22), binarizes weights with x >= 0 ? 1 : -1 (binary_conv_layer.cpp L568), and zero-pads binary convs (standard Caffe conv, pad: 1). The official PyTorch code uses torch.sign (sign(0) = 0) and zero padding (BiReal18_34/birealnet.py L25, L58). The model_conversion.md L37 wording ('existing BNN models which do not have the correct padding value (-1 rather than 0)') suggests zero-padded training, but it is a generic statement.
models.input_spec: 1x3x224x224 NCHW float (ONNX) / 1x224x224x3 NHWC (.dab). Preprocessing is not documented by daBNN. Assumed: Resize 256, CenterCrop 224, ImageNet mean/std as in the official Bi-Real train.py L100-125 (assumption).

The bit-packed .dab uses daBNN's own HWC bit layout, so the ONNX is the cleaner source.

models.architecture:
SSD300 with a binarized VGG16 (ssd/bidet_ssd.py):
- FP conv1_1 + BN.
- 16 BiDetVGGBlocks (binary 3x3 conv + BN + identity residual). The 4 max-pool positions ('M','M','C','M') are replaced by binary 3x3 stride-2 convs whose shortcut is AvgPool + FP 1x1 conv + BN; these blocks also change channel width.
- pool5 MaxPool(3,1,1).
- conv6: binary 3x3, dilation 6, + BN + ReLU.
- conv7: FP 1x1 + BN + ReLU.
- L2Norm on the conv4_3 output.
- 8 binary extras + BN (no residual).
- 6 FP loc/conf 3x3 heads; loc outputs 8 per prior (4 'sigma' + 4 mean); Detect uses [:, :, 4:].
models.dataset: Train VOC07+12 trainval; test VOC2007 test

reported_metrics.value: README (2021-04-19 update) and paper Table (SSD300, VGG16, 'BiDet (SC)', 21.88MB): 66.0% mAP on VOC07 test. Plain BiDet without the extra shortcut is 52.4. The eval script uses the VOC07 11-point metric (use_07=True).

precision.per_layer:
- conv1_1: FP + BN (no ReLU).
- VGG body: binary (BinarizeConv2d) + BN + FP identity residual. The VGG body has no ReLU.
- Stride-2 transitions: binary 3x3 s2 main path + FP shortcut (AvgPool + FP 1x1 + BN).
- pool5: MaxPool.
- conv6: binary dilated 3x3 + BN + ReLU.
- conv7: FP 1x1 (bias) + BN + ReLU.
- L2Norm: FP.
- Extras: binary + BN, no residual, no ReLU.
- loc/conf heads: FP 3x3 with bias.
- Softmax, prior decoding and NMS: FP.

models.binarization_semantics:
ssd/binary_utils.py BinarizeConv2d (l.64-93):
- Activations: SignTwoOrders (input.sign(), so sign(0)=0; Bi-Real ApproxSign backward).
- Weights: mean|W| per out-channel (over dims 1,2,3) * sign(W).
- No activation scale.
- PADDING: F.pad(input, ..., mode='constant', value=-1), then conv2d(padding=0). Binary convs pad with -1. This also applies to the stride-2 and dilated (pad 6) convs and to the stride-2 extras.
- Bias False.
- IMPORTANT: extras.0 consumes the conv7+BN+ReLU output, so its binarized input is in {0,+1} (sign(0)=0). A runtime with sign(0)=+1 would change semantics there.
models.input_spec: Corrected. cv2.imread (BGR), cv2.resize to 300x300, subtract MEANS (104,117,123) in BGR order (ssd/data/config.py:10), no std scaling, then channels swapped to RGB (ssd/data/voc0712.py:137) before the tensor is built. The network input is RGB-ordered. 21 classes. Eval defaults (eval_voc.py): confidence 0.01, NMS IoU 0.45, top_k 200.

license.code: MIT (Copyright (c) 2019 Ziyi Wu); GitHub API reports MIT
license.weights: no explicit weights licence (inherits repo licence? unverified)

models.reference_impl: PyTorch: ssd/bidet_ssd.py + ssd/binary_utils.py + ssd/layers (PriorBox, Detect). Old torch API (Variable). The eval script assumes CUDA by default (--cuda flag). Not executed.
models.conversion_notes:
Needs:
- Binary conv with -1 padding, which is natural for bit-packed ±1 kernels (good fit).
- Dilated binary conv (d=6).
- A {0,1}-input case at extras.0: either sign(0)=0 ternary semantics, or a check that no exact zeros occur (they will, after ReLU).
- AvgPool/MaxPool, L2Norm, SSD priors and NMS.
The large FP heads, conv7 and the FP 1x1 shortcuts are substantial FP compute.
models.known_limitations: Only SSD300-VOC trained weights are released. The loc head predicts 8 values (sigma + mean) and only [:, :, 4:] is used. Evaluation needs VOC2007 test and the VOC07 metric.

extras.0 input is post-ReLU, so it binarizes to {0,1}

precision.per_layer:
FP:
- First conv 3x3 s2 + BN (backbone.feature.0).
- project_mat/project_seg 1x1.
- The second conv of OutputBlock (nn.Conv2d + BN + ReLU).
- Refiner box_filter (depthwise 3x3) and final 1x1 conv.
- BN, PReLU, bilinear upsampling.
Binary: all encoder BasicBlock 3x3/1x1 convs, LRASPP convs, decoder conv/conv_1x1, ConvGRU gates, refiner hidden 1x1 convs.
Encoder blocks have FP residuals (AvgPool on stride-2, no conv). Decoder binary convs have no identity shortcut (BN + LearnableBias + PReLU only).

models.binarization_semantics:
model/mobilenet.py:
- BinaryActivation (l.52-61): torch.sign forward (sign(0)=0), clipped STE, preceded by LearnableBias (move11/move21 in the encoder; LearnableBias in decoder Sequentials).
- BiConv2d (l.8-26): W centred per out-channel (mean over in,kh,kw), scale = per-out-channel mean|W_c|, binary weight scale*sign(W_c). F.conv2d with zero padding.
- channel_threshold is an nn.Parameter saved in the state_dict but UNUSED in forward.
- Encoder: BN after conv, + residual, then LearnableBias + PReLU + LearnableBias (RPReLU).
models.input_spec: RGB frames in [0,1]. The backbone applies ImageNet normalize (0.485,0.456,0.406)/(0.229,0.224,0.225) internally. Recurrent states r1-r4. Optional downsample_ratio + refiner.

precision.per_layer:
FP: fution (1x1 + bias), conv_in, conv_out, LayerNorm (PreNorm), AvgPool in Down, bilinear interpolation in Up, the standalone RPReLUs in FeedForward.
Binary: every conv inside the body, including embedding/mapping 3x3, Down/Up 3x3 branches, Fusion 1x1 branches, and the FeedForward 1x1 and grouped 3x3 (groups=dim). Every binary conv has its own FP identity residual and RPReLU.

models.binarization_semantics:
simulation/test_code/architecture/BiSRNet.py:
- BinaryConv2d (l.84-107): ReDistribution (x*k + b, per channel learned), then Spectral_Binary_Activation (torch.sign forward, sign(0)=0; tanh(beta*x) STE with learned beta), then HardBinaryConv (per-out-channel mean|W| * sign(W), no centring, zero padding, groups supported), then RPReLU, then + x.
- Binary convs always have in_channels = out_channels.
- Channel increase (Fusion_Increase, Down) = duplicate the input into two binary branches and concat (Down applies AvgPool first).
- Channel decrease (Fusion_Decrease, Up) = split channels into halves, apply two binary branches, then AVERAGE (out1+out2)/2. Up applies bilinear x2 first.
models.input_spec: Measurement y and masks Phi: input [b,28,256,256] shifted measurement concatenated with Phi (56 ch). 28 spectral bands, 256x256. KAIST 10 test scenes (TSA_simu_data masks). If Phi is None, the code substitutes torch.rand(...).cuda().

checkpoint.download_status: Re-verified: file present, sha256 and size match; HTTP HEAD 200 (227665054)

models.architecture: AlexNet variant (NCHW graph, NHWC-style kernels): conv0 12x12/4 VALID fp+bias -> activate (no BN); conv1 5x5 SAME split=2 -> BN -> maxpool 3/2 SAME -> act; conv2 3x3 -> BN -> maxpool SAME -> act; conv3 3x3 split=2 -> BN -> act; conv4 3x3 split=2 -> BN -> maxpool VALID -> act; fc0 9216->4096 (+bias) -> BN -> act; fc1 4096->4096 (no bias) -> BN -> clip(0,1); fct 4096->1000 fp + bias

reported_metrics.value: README: top-1 validation error 51.5% (i.e. 48.5% top-1 acc)

precision.per_layer: conv0 fp weights + bias, output clip+1-bit quantized directly (no BN); conv1-4, fc0, fc1: binary weights with a single per-layer scalar E on {0,1} activations; fc0 bias fp; BN fp after each; maxpool on real-valued BN output before quantization; fc1 -> BN -> clip(0,1) (not quantized) -> fct fp

models.binarization_semantics: Weights: where(W==0, 1, sign(W/E))*E with E=mean|W| over the whole tensor (dorefa.py:25-32), so sign(0)=+1 and there is one scalar per layer (also for grouped convs). Activations: fa(clip(x,0,1)) = round(x*1)/1 -> {0,1} (dorefa.py quantize; alexnet-dorefa.py nonlin/activate); tf.round is half-to-even, so 0.5 -> 0. Conv SAME zero padding (0 is a legal {0,1} value). Grouped convs (split=2). 'conv0' and 'fct' are not quantized (alexnet-dorefa.py:77)
models.input_spec: 224x224 BGR uint8, resize shortest edge 256 + centre crop 224, (img - mean*255)/(std*255) with ImageNet mean/std reversed to BGR (imagenet_utils.py:386-396, image_bgr=True)

license.weights: no explicit weights licence (inherits repo licence? unverified)

models.reference_impl: TF1 + tensorpack (alexnet-dorefa.py --load --dorefa 1,1,32); TF 2.16 in env 'lce' but tensorpack not installed; not run
models.conversion_notes: Activations are {0,1}, not ±1: dot = popcount(a AND w+) - popcount(a AND w-) = 2*popcount(a AND w+) - popcount(a). Grouped convs; SAME maxpool on real values before the quantizer (fold BN+pool+quant carefully: maxpool commutes with a monotone threshold only if BN gamma>0); big FC (9216x4096). A reasonable second-tier ImageNet target
models.known_limitations: Low accuracy; legacy TF1 reference; HTTPS endpoint timed out (HTTP works)

evidence.claim: activations {0,1}, scalar weight scale, first/last fp, fc0 has bias

bitino.numerical_verification: passed (host + emulated arm64); physical device pending
bitino.verification_details: Reference: official tensorpack graph (tensorpack 0.11 + TF 2.15.1 CPU, example files unmodified) = reference_logits.f32; fp64 reference = cited PyTorch port tools/dorefa_alexnet_reference.py (official fp32 vs port fp32: max 1.5e-5 on clean samples; eval5000 top-1 differences official32-vs-port64 64, port32-vs-port64 61 = fp32 noise floor). fp64 IR vs fp64 port: 0/128 <= 1e-6, 128/128 <= 1e-4 (max 3.1e-6), 0 binarization flips; float64 constants: 128/128 <= 2.2e-13. Bit-exact with numpy: host reference, neon, neon_unfused, emulated neon; host optimized --explain PASS (0), emulated optimized --explain PASS (1 disagreement, first flip at |pre| 6.3e-7 = 1.0e-6 x typical). Re-validated on master after merge (2a00ae7): host neon bit-exact with numpy, host optimized --explain PASS.
bitino.semantic_notes: DoReFa 1-bit activations round(clip(x,0,1)) = [x > 0.5] -> u = (1+s)/2, s = gt(x, 0.5); weights where(W==0,1,sign W)*E (E = mean|W| per layer): BConv2D/BDense gt, threshold 0.5, pad_value -1 (= zero padding of u), post_mul E/2, post_add E/2*sum w (+ fc0 bias); grouped conv1/3/4; maxpool (TF SAME pads) on the BN output before the quantizer; fc0 rows permuted NCHW->NHWC; single exact variant. Eval set tensorpack_bgr (cv2 BGR, ResizeShortestEdge 256 cubic, crop 224, (x-mean)*fl32(1/std) = TF graph after grappler's division rewrite; bit-identical to the graph's image_preprocess).

reproduced_metrics.note: 100-class ImageNet subset (smoke/regression, not an ImageNet-1k estimate); the official graph gives the same accuracy on it

paper.title: High-Capacity Expert Binary Networks

models.authors: Adrian Bulat, Brais Martinez, Georgios Tzimiropoulos
models.provenance: official authors (README section 2 "Testing pretrained model" links the packed model on adrianbulat.com)

checkpoint.download_status: HTTP 200 (last-modified 2021-01-08), curl full download, size equals content-length
checkpoint.inspection: torch.load(weights_only=True) OK, bare state_dict: 502 tensors (457 fp32, 45 int64), 43,386,041 elements. Stem conv1.0 (32,3,3,3), conv2_1.0 (16,32,1,1), conv2_2.0 (32,16,3,3), conv3.0 (64,64,1,1) FP. Every block conv is 5-D (4 experts, Cout, Cin/g, k, k), e.g. layer1.0.conv1.weight (4,128,16,3,3) (grouped), layer1.0.conv3.weight (4,128,128,1,1); each has alpha2 (1,Cout,1,1), gating fc.weight (4,Cin) and se_fc.{0,2} (C/8 bottleneck). Downsample paths (downsample.1 / downsample.4) are EBConvs too.

models.architecture: "EB-ResNet": 3-conv FP stem (32/16/32/64 channels, 3x3 and 1x1); residual stages built from Expert Binary Convolutions (EBConv2d): each conv holds 4 experts (weight shape (4, Cout, Cin/groups, k, k)), an FP gating Linear (C->4) on the globally pooled input picks one expert per sample (argmax), grouped binary 3x3/1x1 convs, per-channel alpha2 scale and an FP squeeze-excite (se_fc) channel rescale; binary downsample convs (also EBConv); FP classifier

reported_metrics.value: Paper: up to 71.2% top-1 on ImageNet for the best EBConv model (author claim); which configuration this packed model corresponds to is not stated in the README (unverified)

precision.per_layer: Stem convs, gating FC, SE FC, BN, PReLU/activations and classifier: FP. Block convs (3x3 grouped and 1x1) and downsample convs: binary weights and binary activations, scaled by per-channel alpha2 and an SE rescale.

models.binarization_semantics: test/model.py EBConv2d.forward (l.88-140): gate = activation(fc(avgpool(x))); expert index = argmax(gate) per sample (l.103); weight = sign(expert weight) (l.100); x = sign(x) with an assert that every element is +-1 (l.122-125) so sign(0) never occurs in the test model; conv padding is the zero padding of F.conv2d (padding param) applied after sign, so borders are 0 (ternary). Output multiplied by alpha2 (l.136) and by the SE scale (l.138-140). BConv2d (l.9-27) used where num_experts=1: sign on input and weight.
models.input_spec: 224x224 RGB ImageNet (test/test.py; standard resize 256/center-crop 224 assumed, not re-checked)

license.weights: unspecified (MIT repo, weights on personal site)

models.reference_impl: PyTorch, test/model.py (packed inference model, 670 lines) + test/test.py; needs the "bnn" pip package only for training code
models.conversion_notes: Data-dependent expert selection (argmax of an FP gate per sample, i.e. dynamic weights), grouped binary convs, per-channel alpha and SE rescaling. Each expert set can be pre-packed to 1 bit; runtime must select one of 4 weight banks per layer per image. Zero padding after sign gives ternary borders.
models.known_limitations: Exotic op set (dynamic expert routing, SE) not covered by a standard ReActNet adapter; exact accuracy of this file unknown.

evidence.claim: 5-D expert weights with 4 experts and gating FC

bitino.reason: needs new ops: data-dependent expert (weight-bank) selection per sample; grouped BConv2D; SE; eval data: eval128 `torchvision_imagenet` (exists)

models.binarization_semantics: utils/quantization.py: FastSign=torch.sign (sign(0)=0) for weights (no weight scaling, BN follows). QuantSign 2-bit activations clamp[-1,1] -> {-1,-1/3,1/3,1}, which are never 0. PGBinaryConv2d (l.152-191): MSB conv = conv(sign(x), sign(W))*2/3; mask = MSB > learned per-channel threshold; output = (1-mask)*MSB + mask*conv(x_2bit, sign(W)). Zero padding (padding_mode 'zeros'), so padded border positions are 0. Block (model/fracbnn_imagenet.py:71-77): rprelu(BN(PGconv3x3(Q2(x)))) + shortcut(Q4(x)), where the shortcut is AvgPool for stride 2, then shiftbn BN; then pointwise PGconv1x1 + BN + RPReLU + Q4 shortcut (channel duplicate when doubling), then shiftbn. Shortcuts are quantized to 4 bits. Input: denormalize -> thermometer encode (resolution 8, 32 levels x 3 ch = 96 ch, ±1) -> BinaryConv2d (sign weights) + BN.
models.input_spec: 224x224; standard ImageNet Resize256/CenterCrop224/Normalize (imagenet.py:67-95), and the model denormalizes internally before thermometer encoding

models.binarization_semantics: Activations use FakeQuantize levels=2 with per-channel input_low==input_high (a pure threshold) and output {0,1}. OpenVINO FQ maps x<=thr to 0, so a value exactly at the threshold becomes 0, which BC reads as -1. Two threshold types: positive thresholds on post-ReLU/MaxPool block inputs (e.g. 0.049..0.288 in the first block), and thresholds applied directly to a BC output with BN/scales folded in. BinaryConvolution uses mode=xnor-popcount (out=2P-B, with 0 read as -1) and pad_value=-1, which is zero padding in the original {0,1} activation domain. After the last BC of each block: y*0.5 + c, where c==0.5*sum(w) per out channel exactly (verified, check_offset.py). The IR therefore computes sum(w*a) with a in {0,1} and w in {-1,+1}. Then one scalar weight scale (e.g. 0.7346), one scalar activation scale (e.g. 0.08846) and a per-channel BN affine. This is consistent with NNCF DoReFa (per-conv mean|W|) plus out=s*H(in-s*t) (inferred). Sources: OpenVINO binary-convolution-1.rst and fake-quantize-1.rst; IR xml layers id 12-46.
models.input_spec: [1,3,224,224] NCHW, BGR, 0..255. accuracy-check.yml: pillow resize shorter side 256 (bilinear), center crop 224, rgb_to_bgr. Mean subtraction (103.5,116.3,123.7) is embedded in the IR (Subtract). No explicit std, presumably folded into the stem (not verified).

models.binarization_semantics: imagenet/modules/binarized_modules.py:31-68. Weights: w2 = (w - mean)/std per out-channel (unbiased std); w3 = w2 + |sin(rotate)| * (R1^T X R2 - w2); bw = torch.sign(w3), so sign(0)=0. Activations: a2 = (a - mean)/std per sample over (C,H,W), then torch.sign. Equivalently sign(a - per-sample mean), since std>0. Zero padding is applied after sign in F.conv2d. Output * alpha (learned per out-channel). Rotation buffers update only when module.epoch > -1 (training), so inference is static. Block (models_imagenet/resnet.py BasicBlock): conv -> BN -> (+residual, downsample on the first block) -> Hardtanh, repeated for conv2.

reported_metrics.value: SST-2 dev acc 88.7, no data augmentation. The BiBERT README cites this from the paper's Table 1 ablation (77.6 -> 88.7); the BiT README per-task table (BiBERT row) lists it too. 90.9 with data augmentation (BiT README table). Not re-evaluated.

precision.per_layer: Word embedding: binary, per-row alpha=mean|W_row| (uncentered), sign of the per-row-centered W. Position + token-type embeddings: FP32. Embedding LayerNorm: FP32. Q/K/V/O, FFN1, FFN2 and pooler linears: binary weights (per-output-row alpha) x sign activations (no scale), + FP32 bias. Attention: sign(Q+bq)·sign(K+bk)^T/8 + mask(-10000), softmax REMOVED, probs = 1 if score>0 else 0 (score==0 -> 0); V = sign(V+bv); context = {0,1}x{-1,0,+1} integer matmul, then sign()-ed at the O-proj input (ties at 0 -> 0). Residual adds + post-LN LayerNorm: FP32. GELU: FP32 (sign(GELU(x)) == sign(x) except FP32 underflow, see semantics). Pooler: W1A1 dense + FP tanh. Classifier: nn.Linear FP32.

models.binarization_semantics: transformer/utils_quant.py:219-226 (QuantizeLinear.forward): alpha = mean(|W|, dim=1) on the UNcentered W (detached); Wb = alpha*sign(W - mean_row(W)). utils_quant.py:230-233: activations sign(x), no scale/threshold/bias, STE clip [-1,1]. torch.sign(0)=0 for both weights and activations. Embedding uses the same path (utils_quant.py:259-266, dim=1 = per vocab row). Attention: modeling_quant.py:141-184 (BertSelfAttention.forward) applies BinaryQuantizer (sign) to Q and K after the linear+bias. ZMeanBinaryQuantizer (utils_quant.py:28-35) is sign() with -1 set to 0, so score==0 -> 0. Ternary corner cases a strict XNOR port must handle or measure: (a) scores are even integers/8 for ±1 vectors over 64 dims, so exactly 0 is common -> prob 0; (b) the context integer can be 0 -> sign 0 at attention.output.dense input; (c) FFN2 input is sign(GELU(x)), and FP32 erf-GELU underflows to (-)0 for x <= -5.546 -> sign 0. That FFN1 pre-activation range is reachable (row bound 768*alpha+|b| ~ 24); its frequency was not measured. No padding (linear layers only). No BN; post-LN BERT. Classifier FP (modeling_quant.py:521, nn.Linear).

models.conversion_notes: Latent FP32 weights: the converter must center per row, take sign, pack bits, and store alpha per row (alpha from the uncentered |W|). Bool attention without softmax maps to integer ops (XNOR-popcount for Q·K, AND/popcount for {0,1}x{±1}). For bit-exactness, the reference has three-valued (zero) cases: 36 zero weights, score==0, context==0 and GELU underflow. Either carry a zero mask or define 0->+1 and measure the accuracy delta. Biases, LayerNorm, GELU, tanh and the embedding sum stay in FP. 768/3072 are multiples of 64/128, which suits NEON packing.
models.known_limitations: Accuracy far below FP BERT on harder tasks; SST-2 is the strongest task. Stray deps in repo (matplotlib, seaborn, pdb). The reference semantics are not strictly binary at sign(0).

precision.per_layer: Word embedding binary (BWN non-layerwise: per-row scale, GLOBAL-mean centering). Pos/type embeddings FP. Q/K/V/O/FFN/pooler linears: binary weights (single scalar per matrix) x binary activations (signed alpha*sign(x+b) for Q/K/V/O/FFN1/pooler inputs; FFN2 input post-ReLU unsigned {0,alpha}). Q,K,V outputs signed binary; FP softmax, then probs unsigned {0,alpha}. FP rank-1 estimators (768->1 linears on the FP hidden state): their score terms are added before /sqrt(64) and shared across heads, and the v_p term is added to the context. LayerNorms, residuals, pooler tanh + residual, MLM head FP.

models.binarization_semantics: binary_finetune/utils_quant.py and binary_pretraining/utils_quant.py (BiT-derived; they differ only by an unused PReLU and the HalfQuantizeLinear class). BwnQuantizer layerwise: m=||W||_1/numel, sign(W - mean(W))*m. Non-layerwise (embedding): per-row m, global mean e (utils_quant.py:188-192). ElasticQuantBinarizerSigned alpha*sign(x) (sign(0)=0); Unsigned alpha*clamp(round(x/alpha),0,1). QuantizeLinear.forward applies LearnableBias 'move' per input channel before quantization. Config: run_pretrain_binary.py:340-352 and binary_finetune/binary_bert.py:1261-1278 (weight_bits=1, input_bits=1, bwn, elastic, sym_quant_qkvo=True, sym_quant_ffn_attn=False, hidden_act relu; improve_kqv=True and lora_rank=1 set at binary_bert.py:1275-1278). Attention (binary_pretraining/bipft.py:256-263; binary_finetune/binary_bert.py:288-340): scores = sign-binary QK^T + (q_m·k_p^T + q_p·k_m^T + q_p·k_p^T), then /sqrt(64) + mask, softmax, binarize probs; context = probs_b·V_b + probs_b·v_p(h), a per-token scalar broadcast to all 64 head dims. The head count of 12 is hard-coded. Pooler (bipft.py:604-605) = tanh(LayerNorm(binary_dense(cls)) + cls).

models.binarization_semantics: transformer/utils_quant.py BwnQuantizer: with layerwise=True (weights) m=||W||_1/numel and Wb = sign(W - mean(W))*m. With layerwise=False (word embedding, embed_layerwise=False) the scale is per row (||W_row||_1/768), but the centering e = input.mean() is GLOBAL. ElasticQuantBinarizerSigned: alpha*sign(x) (sign(0)=0). Unsigned: alpha*clamp(round(x/alpha),0,1), i.e. threshold alpha/2 with round-half-even (x == alpha/2 -> 0). QuantizeLinear.forward adds LearnableBias 'move' (per input channel) before activation quant. modeling_bert_quant.py:224-229: move_q/k/v are computed but the results are discarded (issue #1, open). Defaults: quant_task_distill_glue.py sym_quant_qkvo=True, sym_quant_ffn_attn=False, weight_layerwise=True, embed_layerwise=False, input_layerwise=True, ACT2FN relu; scripts/run_glue.sh uses --weight_quant_method bwn --input_quant_method elastic --learnable_scaling.

precision.per_layer: Stem: fp Conv2d 3->64 k4 s4 with bias, then BN (BatchNormT), GELU, and an fp 2D position embedding. Body linears (Q/K/V, attention output dense, MLP fc1/fc2) and the token-mixer 3x3 grouped (g=4) dilated (1/3/5) convs are W1A1. Downsample (patch_embed1-3) runs: BN, learned shift, W1A1 2x2 s2 conv, BN, fp AvgPool2d residual with channels repeated, RPReLU, and an fp per-stage position embedding. Attention: Q/K/V binarized with sign, so QK^T is binary x binary with an fp 1/sqrt(d) scale. Softmax is fp. Attention probs are 2-bit (4 levels, per-head learned scale and offset), so AV is 2-bit x binary. Norms: BatchNorm everywhere (replace_ln_bn), except one real fp nn.LayerNorm in Token_for_Attention per attention layer. Shortcuts, all fp: Q/K/V input residual, context + q + k + v sum, MLP shortcuts (fc1 channel repeat, fc2 channel AvgPool1d), RPReLU, LayerScale, circular torch.roll shift branches (shift3/shift5), token-split blend. Head: BN, token mean-pool, fp Linear 512->1000.

models.binarization_semantics: sign: torch.sign, so sign(0)=0 (transformer/utils_quant.py:10). Weights in QuantizeLinear: W_b = mean(|W|, dim=1, un-centred) * sign(W - mean(W, dim=-1)), per out-row (utils_quant.py:216-218). QuantizeConv2d: scale = mean |W| over [1,2,3]; centre over [1,2,3] (utils_quant.py:338-347). The exact-zero centred weights are float32 rounding artefacts: 2 on CPU fp32, 0 in fp64; the count depends on hardware and reduction order. Activations: sign(x + move) with a learned per-channel shift and no activation scale (BHViT.py:192-194, 260, 303, 325, 423, 616). Q/K/V are sign(RPReLU(BN(binlinear(x+move)) + x) + move2) (BHViT.py:192-210). Binary convs use F.conv2d with padding='same' on the binarized input, so the pad value is 0 (not +/-1); padding correction is needed (utils_quant.py:368; BHViT.py:414-416). Downsample conv: 2x2 s2, no bias, padding 0. Attention-prob quantizer: q = round(3P/alpha_h + zp_h).clamp(0,3) and out = q*alpha_h; zp is NOT subtracted on dequantisation (BHViT.py:159, 222; utils_quant.py:565-570). BN placement: BN directly follows every binary linear and the downsample conv. In the token mixer, each of the 3 convs goes through its own RPReLU; the branches are summed, then one BN (BHViT.py:420-431).

ActBi (Bi_Quant.py:162-200), eval: zp_r = round(zero_point) (round-half-even); out = (sign(clamp(x/alpha + zp_r, -1, 1)) - zp_r) * alpha, with a per-head alpha that can be negative. For attention probs with zp_r=-1 and alpha>0 the code is {0, 2*alpha} with threshold alpha. Attention zero points sit at about +/-1.4999, right on the rounding boundary between +/-1 and +/-2, so fp16 storage or a different round mode changes the codes; precompute zp_r from fp32. No BN. models.architecture: resnet18_mtf_msf_ours. Siamese Bi-Real-style ResNet-18 encoder with 16 single-conv blocks ([4,4,4,4]) and shared weights. MTF (only the 'exchange' branch is live), an FPN over 4 levels with fpn_channel=512, and a binary ASPP DeepLab head with 2 classes. The training-only aux decoders are included in the checkpoint.
models.dataset: PCD (TSUNAMI/GSV, cross-validation fold 0), input 256 for training and (224,1024) for testing

reported_metrics.value: Paper Table 1 (author claim), 1-bit C-3PO+BiCD on PCD: F1 GSV 74.1, TSUNAMI 86.5; 2.1M params, 6.6 G OPs. tips.txt says this best.pth was selected on GSV, not TSUNAMI. log.txt epoch 99: TSUNAMI F1 0.8543 (IoU 81.48), GSV F1 0.7273 (IoU 71.11).

precision.per_layer: Stem: FP conv7x7 s2 + BN + maxpool. Encoder body: W1A1 (sign, binary 3x3 with mean|W| scale, BN, FP residual add). Downsample: AvgPool2d + binary-weight 1x1 on FP activations (W1A-fp) + BN. MTF exchange: |f0-f1| then binary-weight 3x3 on FP input (W1A-fp), BN, residual, ReLU. FPN cf_inners/cf_layers: W1A1 with BN and FP residual. ASPP: 4 W1A1 dilated convs (ReCU-normalized weights, bias) with BN, residual and RPReLU. Channel attention: binary-weight 1x1 on pooled FP vectors (W1A-fp) with PReLU and sigmoid. Channel avg-pool reduce and BN in FP. Head: FP 3x3 conv to 2 classes, then bilinear upsample. Aux decoders: FP, training-only (removed at deployment per the paper).

models.binarization_semantics: Activations use torch.sign, so sign(0)=0 (BinaryActivation and BinaryQuantizer, src/model/binary_version_HFA_blank_decoder/utils_quant.py ~l.57-75 and ~l.420+). HardBinaryConv (~l.31-54) computes mean|W| per output channel x sign(W) with an STE clamp of +/-1. QuantizeConv2d (ASPP) centers W per output channel, normalizes by std/(2*sqrt2), takes sign and scales by mean|W| of the un-centered weights; activations are sign(x + learnable move bias) and a bias is added. QuantizeConv2dwoact: sign(W) x mean|W| post-scaling on FP input. The encoder has no learnable threshold (move0 unused) and no RPReLU. Padding: zero padding on the {-1,0,+1} sign map. BN sits after every binary conv, before the residual add. All residual and shortcut paths are FP.
models.input_spec: Two RGB images concatenated to 6 channels (split 3+3), ImageNet mean/std normalization (src/dataset/dataset.py ~l.84). Resized to 256 for training and (224,1024) for PCD testing.

Needs W1A-fp binary-weight convs on FP inputs (downsample, MTF exchange, channel attention), channel-dim AvgPool1d reductions (permute plus pool), dilated binary convs with d=12/24/36, and a sigmoid channel attention. Dead branches (cfs conv/res/ca1, aux decoders, encoder fc) can be pruned. Binary weights must be pre-binarized from latent weights using the ReCU centering for the ASPP convs.

precision.per_layer: SimpleUNet: intro 3x3 and ending 3x3 FP; downs 2x2 s2 FP; ups 1x1+PixelShuffle FP; LayerNorm2d FP; GELU; UNetBlock convs are BConv2d (W1A1); beta/gamma residual scales FP. MainBMTNet: m_head/m_tail 3x3 FP; all down/up sampling convs FP; RFF Fourier encoding FP; intro_qb and qb_fusion FP; intro_fourier_qb binary weights on FP input (W1A-fp); UNetQBConvBlock uses BinaryConv2dSkip1x1 (W1A1 conv plus FP 1x1 conv_skip). Mamba: in/x/dt/out projections BiLinear (W1A1), conv2d BConv2d, selective scan FP, SiLU/LN/softplus/exp FP. Cross-Swin: q/k/v sign-binarized, attention probs binarized to {0,1}, relative position bias FP, MLP BiLinear with FP GELU, LayerNorm FP.

models.binarization_semantics: models/MainBMTNet.py. BiLinear (~l.60-100): weight centered along the input dim, then sign, times a learned per-output scaling_factor (initialized to mean|W| on first run); activation sign(x) without shift; bias always present. HardBinaryConv: mean|W| per output channel x sign(W) + bias. BConv2d: x + move0 bias, sign, binary conv, RPReLU, + x. Sign is torch.sign, so sign(0)=0. Consequence: dt_rank=1 means ld1-4 have in_features=1, W - mean(W) = 0 exactly, the binarized dt weight is all zeros and dt = bias. SoftmaxBinaryQuantizer: probs >= 0.25*max -> 1 else 0. Padding: zero padding on sign maps (HardBinaryConv padding=k//2). No BN; LayerNorm/LayerNorm2d are used instead.
models.input_spec: Quad Bayer RAW .bin (uint16 header width, height; values 0-1023). coarse_inpaint of HybridEVS pixels, divide by 1024; 3-channel qb_map synthesized from the 4x4 pattern; replication padding to a multiple of 64. Output RGB x256 clamped to 0-255. The repo ships input/0801.bin and reference output/0801.png.

precision.per_layer: Stem: FP Conv3x3 s2 (3->32) + BN. Body: every 3x3 and 1x1 conv is binary in both weights and activations (BinaryConv2d). BN after each binary conv. RSign shifts (move11, move21) and RPReLU (move12/PReLU/move13, move22/PReLU/move23) are FP. Residuals: FP identity add after every conv. Downsample: AvgPool2d(2,2) on the shortcut, stride-2 binary 3x3; channel doubling by two binary 1x1 convs concatenated, no FP downsample conv. Head: AdaptiveAvgPool, FP Linear(1024,1024)+ReLU. No ImageNet classifier is shipped; linear eval adds an FP ClsHead Linear(1024,1000).

models.binarization_semantics: openselfsup/models/backbones/reactnet.py:120-146 BinaryConv2d. Activations: input.sign() in eval, SignSTE (binaryfunction.py:4-17, hard-clip STE |x|<=1) in training. torch.sign gives sign(0)=0. Weights: sign(W) * mean|W| over (in,kh,kw), a per-output-channel scale computed at run time from the latent weights (l.137-139). Padding: zero padding through F.conv2d(..., self.padding) (l.144). The comment about padding with -1 is NOT implemented. No conv bias. Learnable thresholds: LearnableBias move11 before binary_3x3 and move21 before the binary 1x1 (RSign); RPReLU = move12->PReLU->move13 and move22->PReLU->move23 (l.180-203, 214-253). BN is placed after the binary conv and before the residual add. The BinaryActivation (ApproxSign) module is instantiated but unused in forward.
models.input_spec: 224x224 RGB. Eval: Resize 256, CenterCrop 224. Normalize mean (0.485,0.456,0.406), std (0.229,0.224,0.225) (configs/benchmarks/linear_classification/imagenet/react_last_full.py)

models.conversion_notes: Standard ops: conv, BN, PReLU, per-channel bias add, avgpool, concat, linear. Binary conv semantics: zero padding with ternary borders (needs a border-correction term like LCE pad_values=0, or else retraining with -1 padding); sign(0)=0 on activations (rare in practice, but bit-packing will map it to +1 or -1, so an ulp-level mismatch is expected). Per-out-channel alpha = mean|W| can be folded into the following BN. The 1024x1024 MLP and any linear head stay FP (or INT8). Latent weights must be packed with sign().

With frozen_stages=14 the backbone fc.0 MLP is not frozen during 'linear' eval (reactnet.py:459-465), so the reported protocol trains fc.0 plus fc_cls (this is my reading of the code).

models.provenance: Official framework zoo reproduction (not the original authors' weights). Release birealnet-v0.3.0 (2019-09-08).

checkpoint.format: Keras HDF5 weights-only (keras 2.2.4-tf), float32. birealnet.json is in the release.
checkpoint.download_status: Re-verified 2026-10-29: sha256 and size match. URL HTTP 200.
checkpoint.inspection: 63 layers, 102 tensors, 11,699,112 elements (equal to the docstring params). 4 conv2d: 7x7x3x64 FP stem plus 3 FP 1x1 shortcuts. 16 quant_conv2d 3x3 (latent within ±1.0). 20 BN, 2/4800 negative gammas. dense (512,1000). 3 average_pooling2d. No zeros in the binary kernels.

models.architecture: Bi-Real Net-18: 16 single-conv residual blocks (filters 64-512). Downsample blocks use a binary 3x3 stride-2 conv on the main path (birealnet.py:25-59).

reported_metrics.value: Top-1 57.47%, top-5 79.84%, 4.03 MB (docstring, birealnet.py:144). Docs table: 57.5/79.8, 4.00 MB, 41.7 ms Pixel 1. LCE README: 41.6 ms Pixel 1, versus 61.3 ms that dabnn reports for a 56.4%-accuracy Bi-RealNet.

precision.per_layer: Stem: FP 7x7 s2 conv, then BN(m 0.8), then MaxPool 3/2 (no ReLU anywhere in the network). Body: W1A1 3x3. Shortcut: identity, or FP AvgPool2 s2 'same' + 1x1 conv + BN in downsample blocks (the main path is then a binary stride-2 conv). Residual add FP. BN FP. Head GAP, then FP Dense with bias.

models.binarization_semantics: Input: approx_sign (forward larq.math.sign, sign(0)=+1; larq quantizers.py:98-107). Weights: magnitude_aware_sign = per-output-channel mean|W| × ste_sign(W) (quantizers.py:455-462, reduce over all axes except the last). The scale can be folded into BN. WeightClip(1.0). padding 'same' with the default pad_values=0, i.e. zero padding of the binarized input (ternary border). Conv, then BN(m=0.8), then add (birealnet.py:17-19,46-59).
models.input_spec: 224x224x3, larq_zoo.preprocess_input

license.weights: No explicit weights licence (inherits repo licence? unverified)

models.reference_impl: TF/Keras + larq, larq_zoo/literature/birealnet.py
models.conversion_notes: LCE converts it (docs latency listed). The per-channel weight scale passes IsBinaryFilter (prepare_tf.cc:66-88, per-output-channel |w/scale|≈1). Zero padding with SAME is supported only on the arm target, and the optimized kernel requires float output with no fused activation (bconv2d.cc:188-199; prepare_patterns_common.td:95-127). Bitino needs zero-pad correction (ternary border) or must accept a mismatch.
models.known_limitations: Zero padding complicates pure XNOR-popcount kernels. The Larq reproduction (57.47%) is slightly HIGHER than the 56.4% Bi-RealNet figure in the LCE README, which attributes 56.4% to dabnn's reference. The original paper's own number was not re-read.

bitino.verification_details: fp64 IR vs fp64 source: 19/128 samples deviate, each traced (8 inspected) to a single sign flip at |pre| <= 2.3e-6 (typical |pre| ~1). C++ host bit-exact with numpy executor on 128/128 samples across stages (exercises zero-padding correction).

models.authors: Shuchang Zhou, Yuxin Wu, Zekun Ni, Xinyu Zhou, He Wen, Yuheng Zou (original); reproduction by Plumerai
models.provenance: Official framework zoo reproduction. Release dorefanet-v0.1.0 (2019-09-25).

checkpoint.inspection: 21 layers, 28 tensors, 62,403,912 elements (equal to the docstring). conv2d (12,12,3,96) with bias, FP. quant_conv2d (5,5,96,256), (3,3,256,384), (3,3,384,384), (3,3,384,256) with unconstrained latent weights (-4.09..4.21). quant_dense (9216,4096) and (4096,4096). dense (4096,1000) with bias. 6 BN without gamma. No zeros.

models.architecture: AlexNet-like: FP 12x12 s4 conv (VALID, bias), 4 quantized convs (256, 384, 384, 256), 2 quantized dense layers (4096), FP dense to 1000 (dorefanet.py:85-102).

reported_metrics.value: Top-1 53.39%, top-5 76.50%, 22.84 MB (docstring). Docs table: 53.4/76.5, 22.80 MB, LCE latency 'Unsupported' (footnote: 'uses quantizers for which currently no optimized implemention is available in Larq Compute Engine').

precision.per_layer: First conv FP (with bias, VALID). It has no BN or activation; its output goes straight into the 2-bit quantizer of the next conv. Quantized convs and the two dense layers use 1-bit weights with a per-layer scale and 2-bit activations (W1A2). BN FP (scale=False). Head: clip_by_value(0,1) activation, then FP Dense with bias, then softmax.

models.binarization_semantics: Activations: larq DoReFa (alias DoReFaQuantizer), k_bit=2, mode 'activations': clip to [0,1], then round(x*3)/3 (larq quantizers.py:549-700; dorefanet.py:41-43). Weights: magnitude_aware_sign_unclipped = per-LAYER mean|W| × larq.math.sign(W), so sign(0)=+1. Identity gradient, no constraint (dorefanet.py:11-24,49). padding 'same' with pad 0 (0 is a valid 2-bit level). Order: conv, BN, then optional MaxPool.
models.input_spec: 224x224x3, larq_zoo.preprocess_input

license.weights: No explicit weights licence (inherits repo licence? unverified)

models.reference_impl: TF/Keras + larq, larq_zoo/literature/dorefanet.py
models.conversion_notes: NOT supported by LCE, per the docs footnote. Needs a W1A2 kernel (2 bit-planes). The QuantDense layers would also need a binary or low-bit GEMM.
models.known_limitations: Not a strict BNN (2-bit activations). Large FP dense head. 250 MB file.

bitino.numerical_verification: passed (host + emulated arm64); device pending; not strict BNN (W1A2)
bitino.verification_details: New ops QBConv2D/QBDense (2-bit DoReFa activations x binary weights, integer accumulation; reference kernels only). fp64: 123/128 <=1e-6, 5 without level change. Neon bit-exact; optimized PASS.

The local file exists, sha256sum and size match the hard-coded hash and the GitHub API asset size (50837992), and the URL returns HTTP 200. quicknet_small.json was also downloaded (sha256 5442b1c9f6487617f379c94b1ec5d8fb51996d5a1527906818f02bab2846e8f6).
checkpoint.inspection: h5py, re-run: 76 layers, 113 tensors, 12,664,344 float32 elements (docstring 12,655,688 params). 21 quant_conv2d: 16 binary 3x3 with latent weights exactly within ±1.25; stem (3,3,3,8) range -4.47..4.69; stem 1x1 (1,1,8,32); FP transition 1x1s (32→64, 64→256, 256→512). 1 quant_depthwise_conv2d (3,3,8,1). 3 blur-pool depthwise kernels with values 0.0625..0.25. 22 BN, 0 negative gammas. quant_dense (512,1000) with bias. No exact zeros in the binary kernels. The JSON confirms pad_values=1.0, activation=relu, SteSign(1.25) and WeightClip(1.25).

models.architecture: QuickNet v1. section_blocks (4,4,4,4), section_filters (32,64,256,512) (quicknet.py:190-192). FP stem: 3x3 s2 conv to 8 ch, then depthwise 3x3 s2, then 1x1 to 32. 16 binary 3x3 residual blocks. Three transitions, each blur-pool plus FP 1x1. FP dense head.

reported_metrics.value: Top-1 59.4%, top-5 81.8%, 12,655,688 params, 4.00 MB (quicknet.py docstring; docs.larq.dev/zoo). Docs: 17.5 ms Pixel 1 single thread (benchmarked 2020-10-15). LCE README, Pixel 1: 16.8 ms (1 thread), 8.9 ms (4 threads). RPi4B 27.7 / 12.1 ms. M1 4.0 / 1.8 ms.

precision.per_layer: Stem FP: QuantConv2D without quantizers, 3x3 s2, then BN, then ReLU; FP depthwise 3x3 s2, then BN(scale=False, center=False); FP 1x1, then BN (quicknet.py:76-105). Body: W1A1 3x3 convs. Residual adds FP. Transition FP: ReLU, MaxPool(2, stride 1, 'valid' padding, so spatial shrinks by 1), fixed blur-pool depthwise 3x3 s2 'same', FP 1x1, BN (:127-152). There is no shortcut around transitions. BN FP. Head: ReLU, AvgPool (global), Flatten, FP QuantDense with bias, softmax.

models.binarization_semantics: Input and weights use SteSign(clip_value=1.25) (quicknet.py:63,67). Forward is larq.math.sign = tf.sign(tf.sign(x)+0.1), so sign(0)=+1 (larq/math.py:25). No weight or activation scaling. WeightClip(1.25) (:71). padding='same' with pad_values=1.0 (:119-120). Padding is applied AFTER input binarization: QuantConv2D MRO is BaseLayer.call (quantize) then QuantizerBaseConv.call (tf.pad with pad_values) (larq/layers_base.py:47-51,164-172). activation='relu' on the bconv output BEFORE BN (:114), then BN(momentum 0.9, eps 1e-5), then x + residual (:123-125). The blur-pool kernel is non-trainable and stored in the h5.
models.input_spec: 224x224x3 RGB NHWC. larq_zoo.preprocess_input (training/data.py:20-34,170-205,231-245): center crop of side int(224/256*min(H,W)), tf.compat.v1.image.resize_bicubic to 224, float32, subtract [0.485,0.456,0.406]*255, divide by [0.229,0.224,0.225]*255.

models.architecture: Pre-v1 QuickNetBase. blocks (6,8,12,6), filters (64,128,256,512). Squeeze-excite in sections 3-4 (use_squeeze_and_excite (F,F,T,T)). fp_pointwise_transition_block. Stem: Conv2D(8, 3x3 s2, no BN or activation), then DepthwiseConv2D(multiplier 8, s2, ReLU), then BN (legacy quicknet.py:12-32, 274-284).

reported_metrics.value: Top-1 67.0%, top-5 87.3%, 22,058,368 params, 6.22 MB (legacy docstring @40f4cdc29f lines 434-436). Not in the current docs table. No LCE latency published.

precision.per_layer: FP stem: conv (no BN or act), then depthwise ×8 with ReLU, then BN. Body W1A1 3x3: SteSign 1.25, pad +1, ReLU, BN. SE attention FP in sections 3-4: GAP of the real-valued block input, then Dense(C/16, ReLU, no bias), then Dense(C, sigmoid, no bias), then reshape; the result multiplies the BN output. Transition: shortcut is FP MaxPool(stride) + 1x1 conv + BN; main path is a binary stride-2 conv to the new width; the two are added. FP residual adds. Head ReLU, GAP, FP Dense with bias.

models.binarization_semantics: SteSign(clip 1.25) on input and weights, sign(0)=+1. No scale. WeightClip 1.25. padding 'Same' with pad_values=1.0. activation relu on the bconv output before BN. SE multiply after BN (legacy quicknet.py:97-121).

checkpoint.inspection: 169 layers, 151 tensors, 11,995,624 elements (equal to the docstring). r2b_bnn_block_1_conv2d (7,7,3,64) FP. r2b_bnn_block_1_prelu alpha (1,1,64) is present, confirming the PReLU stem. 16 binary r2b_bnn_block_{2..9}{a,b}_conv2d 3x3, with latent weights outside ±1 (overall -5.92..9.14). scaling_dense_reduce and scaling_dense_expand per half-block, e.g. 2a (64,8)/(8,64) and 4a (64,8)/(8,128). PReLU alphas (1,1,C). shortcut_conv2d 1x1 at 4a, 6a and 8a. block_10_logits (512,1000) with bias. 20 BN, 4/4352 negative gammas. No zeros in the binary kernels.

models.architecture: Real-to-Binary ResNet-18 style: 8 blocks of 2 half-blocks each (blocks 2-9; downsample at 4, 6, 8), data-dependent SE output scaling, PReLU.

precision.per_layer: Stem: FP 7x7 s2, BN, PReLU, MaxPool 3/2. Half-block: BN (FP), then W1A1 3x3 conv (stride 2 at 4a/6a/8a). The conv output is multiplied by an FP SE scale: GAP of the real-valued BN output, then Dense(C_in/8, ReLU, no bias), then Dense(C_out, sigmoid, no bias). Then PReLU, then add the shortcut. Shortcut: identity, or FP AvgPool2 + 1x1 conv + BN. Head: GAP, FP Dense with bias, softmax.

models.binarization_semantics: ste_sign on input and weights (clip 1.0), sign(0)=+1 (real_to_bin_nets.py:415-420). No weight scaling. Output scaling is data-dependent (:271-305). kernel_constraint 'weight_clip' is declared, but the stored latent weights exceed ±1 (irrelevant for sign). padding 'same' with pad 0. The stem uses PReLU because use_prelu=isinstance(self, StrongBaselineNetFactory) (:100) and RealToBinNetFactory subclasses it, despite the comment at :46. Only r2b_bnn has weights. RealToBinNetBANFactory raises 'only has ImageNet weights for the BNN variant'. RealToBinNetFPFactory does not raise: because of an upstream bug in the :308-311 condition it would load the BNN weights. StrongBaseline* and ResNet18FP raise 'No stored weights' (:125-126).

reported_metrics.value: Top-1 61.67% (drop 8.09 vs FP 69.76), from examples/torch/classification/README.md 'Results for binarization' at v2.5.0 and docs/ModelZoo.md v2.6.0-v2.9.0. The in-checkpoint best_acc1 is 63.846, which is inconsistent with the README; not re-measured.

precision.per_layer: Stem conv1 7x7: FP32 (ignored_scopes). Stem BN/ReLU/maxpool: FP32. Body: 16 3x3 convs with binary weights {-a,+a} (a per output channel = mean|W| over Cin,kh,kw) and binary input activations {0,s} (s learned per-layer scalar, threshold learned per input channel). BN after each conv: FP32. ReLU: FP. Residual add: FP. Downsample 1x1 conv + BN in layer2/3/4 block 0: FP32 (ignored). Global avgpool: FP. fc 512->1000 (+bias): FP32. By my count from layer shapes, about 92.4% of MACs are binarized.

models.binarization_semantics: Weights: sign = (w > 0)*2 - 1, so sign(0) = -1 (nncf/torch/binarization/binarize_functions.py:61; reference.py:202; cpu/functions_cpu.cpp input.gt(0); cuda/functions_cuda_impl.cu:42). XNOR scale = |W|.mean(dims [1,2,3]) (binarize_functions.py:60), i.e. one per output channel. The NNCF docstring and Binarization.md say 'per input channel', but the code reduces over dims 1-3 of [Cout,Cin,kh,kw]. Activations: out = s * (x > s*sigmoid(t)) (binarize_functions.py:122-123; layers.py:133 passes scale.exp() and threshold.sigmoid()), so out is in {0,s} and x exactly at the threshold maps to 0. The stored 'scale' is log(s) and is initialized from the top-0.1% activation value (layers.py:122-131). The stored 'threshold' is a logit with shape (1,Cin,1,1). Binarizer inputs are post-ReLU (torchvision BasicBlock). Padding: NNCFConv2d nncf_padding_value buffer = 0.0 in all 20 convs (nncf/torch/layers.py:125,162-188), so ordinary zero padding, which matches the {0,s} '0' level exactly. BN placement: binconv -> BN -> ReLU (-> add for conv2) -> next binarizer. No RPReLU or learnable bias shift beyond the threshold. Schedule: activations binarized from epoch 10 and weights from epoch 30 (configs/binarization/resnet18_imagenet_binarization_xnor.json).
models.input_spec: 1x3x224x224 RGB. Resize(256) then CenterCrop(224), ToTensor, Normalize mean (0.485,0.456,0.406) std (0.229,0.224,0.225) (examples/torch/classification/main.py:442,469-476).

license.weights: Not stated separately. Presumably Apache-2.0 as part of the NNCF model zoo (unverified).

models.reference_impl: PyTorch + NNCF <= v2.9.0 (nncf/torch/binarization/*). The reference is simple enough to reimplement in plain PyTorch on the host (torchvision resnet18 + XNOR weight fn + scale/threshold act fn from reference.py) without NNCF. Not executed here.
models.conversion_notes: Weights must be binarized offline from the latent FP32 values: bit = w>0, alpha_o = mean|W_o|. Activations are unsigned {0,1}*s, not ±1, so the kernel needs AND+popcount: y = alpha_o * s * (2*popcnt(a & w+) - popcnt(a)). Per-input-channel thresholds s*sigmoid(t_c) become a per-channel compare on the FP (post-ReLU) input, and preceding BN/ReLU can fold into integer thresholds only where no residual add intervenes. log-scale and logit storage must be converted (exp, sigmoid). Stem, downsample 1x1 convs and fc need an FP32/INT8 path. The checkpoint needs stub globals to load with weights_only; strip it to state_dict and export (about 47 MB) before use. ONNX export in NNCF emits custom FakeQuantize(levels=2) nodes in the org.openvinotoolkit domain.
models.known_limitations: Binarization was deprecated in NNCF v2.9.0 and removed in v2.10.0. Files bundle optimizer state (327 MB). There is a 2-point gap between best_acc1 and the README accuracy. Accuracy (61.7%) is well below modern BNNs. The XNOR 'per input channel' doc wording contradicts the code.
